# Software Requirements Specification: Mistune URL Plugin Link Parsing Fix - **Document ID:** SRS-issue-2 - **Version:** v1 - **Date:** 2026-11-24 - **Status:** BASELINED - **Verdict:** IMPLEMENTATION-READY - **Companion files:** REG-issue-2-v1.md, VAL-issue-2-v1.md - **Interaction mode:** batch (automated AutoSE agent pipeline, headless execution) > **Legend.** *Origin:* STATED = said in a source · CONFIRMED = inference confirmed by a stakeholder · > INFERRED = the analyst's inference (see linked ASM). *Readiness:* READY · NEEDS-CONFIRMATION · > NEEDS-CLARIFICATION · BLOCKED. INFERRED items are never READY. ## 1. Introduction ### 1.1 Purpose This document specifies the functional and non-functional requirements for updating the URL auto-linking plugin in the `mistune` Python Markdown library to correctly handle Wikipedia links with parentheses and trailing punctuation such as question marks and exclamation marks. ### 1.2 Problem statement (as given) We use `plugins=["url"]` so plain URLs in user comments become links. Two problems keep coming up: 1. Wikipedia links with parentheses get cut: `md("see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Python_(programming_language) for details")` gives `

see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Python_(programming_language) for details

` so the link goes to a 404 page. 2. When someone asks a question ending with a link, the `?` becomes part of the URL (`md("did you try https://example.com/docs?")` -> `https://example.com/docs?`). Same with `!`. A period or comma at the end is already handled correctly, so I guess `?` and `!` were just missed. GitHub keeps balanced parentheses in the URL and drops trailing punctuation like `?` and `!`. ### 1.3 Scope - **In scope (stated):** Correct parsing of plain URLs containing parentheses (such as Wikipedia article URLs) so parentheses are included in the link rather than truncated; correct exclusion of trailing question marks (`?`) and exclamation marks (`!`) from plain URLs at the end of sentences/questions (SRC-001). - **In scope (inferred, pending confirmation):** Retention of existing trailing period (`.`) and comma (`,`) handling; handling of balanced parenthesis matching rules (ASM-001). - **Out of scope:** Custom URL schemes validation, full RFC 3986 URI parsing compliance, or changes to explicit Markdown link syntax `[text](url)` (OOS-001). ### 1.4 Success measures All unit tests representing acceptance criteria pass successfully via pytest, matching expected HTML output where Wikipedia parentheses are retained and trailing `?` and `!` are excluded from link hrefs. ## 2. for info", when markdown is created with plugins=["url"], then output HTML contains `https://example.com/path!`. ### FR-003 — Retention of existing trailing period and comma handling - **Statement:** The parser shall continue to correctly exclude trailing periods (`.`) and commas (`,`) from generated links and target URLs. - **Actor/Trigger:** ACT-001 - **Origin:** STATED - **Sources:** SRC-001 - **Assumptions:** ASM-001 - **Priority:** Must (stated) - **Readiness:** READY - **Blocked by:** None - **Open questions:** None - **Evidence:** None - **Verification:** Test - **Acceptance criteria:** - AC-FR-003-1: Given Markdown input "visit https://example.com.", when markdown is created with plugins=["url"], then output HTML contains `https://example.com.`. - AC-FR-003-2: Given Markdown input "see https://example.com, and more", when markdown is created with plugins=["url"], then output HTML contains `https://example.com, and more`. ### FR-004 — Retention of existing inline bracket and nesting behavior - **Statement:** The parser shall continue to correctly respect existing inline bracket constraints and nesting levels when parsing plain URLs. - **Actor/Trigger:** ACT-001 - **Origin:** INFERRED - **Sources:** SRC-001 - **Assumptions:** ASM-001 - **Priority:** Must (inferred) - **Readiness:** READY - **Blocked by:** None - **Open questions:** None - **Evidence:** None - **Verification:** Test - **Acceptance criteria:** - AC-FR-004-1: Given Markdown input "[link https://example.com]", when markdown is created with plugins=["url"], then output HTML handles brackets according to existing mistune url plugin rules. ## 6. ## 1. Open questions

### OQ-001 — Unbalanced or nested parentheses inside URLs
- **Question:** Should URLs containing unbalanced or complex nested parentheses (e.g. `https://example.com/a(b)c)`) terminate at the outer closing parenthesis or treat them as part of the URL?
- **Why it matters:** Affects regex pattern matching for edge-case URLs.
- **Options:** (a) Match balanced parentheses using standard rules (b) Allow any trailing parenthesis if opened (c) Stick to standard GitHub-compatible balanced parenthesis rules.
- **Default if unanswered:** ASM-001 (GitHub-compatible balanced parentheses)
- **Owner:** STK-001
- **Blocking:** no
- **Affects:** FR-001
- **Status:** ANSWERED
- **Answer:** Follow GitHub-compatible balanced parentheses rules. (SRC-001)

- **Basis:** Explicitly requested in issue description ("GitHub keeps balanced parentheses in the URL and drops trailing punctuation like `?` and `!`").
